title: 2d — Making Programs Dynamic

content.title: Reusing variables
content.summary: Change a variable once at the top and the whole program updates automatically.
content.body: Once a variable exists, you can use it as many times as you like. Change the variable once at the top and the whole program updates — you never have to search through every line.

content.title: Combining text with +
content.summary: Use + to glue a variable and a string together into one line of output.
content.body:
You can join a variable and a string together using +. Python glues them into one line of text.

name = "Mia"
print(name + " entered the castle.")

Output: Mia entered the castle.

content.title: Watch the spaces
content.summary: Python won't add spaces for you — include them inside the string: " entered the castle."
content.body: When joining text with +, Python won't add spaces for you. Make sure to include a space at the start of the string: " entered the castle." — see the space before 'entered'?

editorPrompt: Use a variable and + to print a message that includes a name.
progressiveHints:
# Starter code — try changing the name or the message!
name = "Mia"
print(name + " entered the castle.")

# Hint: Use + to combine a variable with extra text
# print(name + " found a treasure chest!")

name = "Mia"
item = "golden key"
print(name + " found a " + item + "!")

name = "Mia"
item = "golden key"
room = "the dragon's lair"
print(name + " entered " + room + ".")
print(name + " picked up the " + item + ".")
print("The door slammed shut!")
